title: TRACI: Network Acceleration of Input-Dynamic Communication for Large-Scale Deep Learning Recommendation Model
problem: Multi-GPU DLRM training is bottlenecked by embedding layer communication: the Aggregation collective (sparse, input-dependent gather/reduce across GPUs) cannot be accelerated by existing in-network compute solutions designed for All-Reduce because its data transfer patterns are dynamic and depend on input batch content, not topology.
motivation: DLRM embedding tables are terabyte-scale and require high memory bandwidth; multi-GPU scaling is necessary but Aggregation communication becomes the binding bottleneck as All-Reduce solutions do not apply to input-dynamic sparse patterns.
method: TRACI adds tags to messages that GPUs send when requesting embeddings, marking when multiple requests need the same data (input-reuse) and when data has already been retrieved (output-reuse). Network switches read these tags and recognize duplicate requests, combining them instantly so each unique request is processed just once and the results are sent to all GPUs that need them, rather than routing every request separately to a host.
key_novelty: Using metadata tags on embedding requests to mark identical requests (input-reuse) and available results (output-reuse), enabling network switches to combine duplicates on-the-fly instead of routing all requests to a host.
contributions: Analysis of Aggregation as a distinct communication bottleneck in multi-GPU DLRM that existing in-network solutions cannot address.
Novel network transaction type augmenting messages with reuse identifiers to expose embedding lookup sharing to the network.
Custom switch hardware design that discovers and exploits message connections dynamically for in-network Aggregation.
Demonstrated network communication reduction for multi-GPU DLRM training.
